system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Senior Backend Engineer | Python, Go
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior backend engineer with 21 years of experience building production services and large-scale distributed
systems in Python, Go and C++. Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service handling 120k requests
per second, and led technical work on a playback API and a migration from a Python 2 monolith to around 60
Python and Go services; playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%. Experienced with PostgreSQL,
backend APIs, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform and observability tooling. Fluent in English and experienced in
documenting architecture.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH, Munich 2019 – August 2026
• Led the technical migration of a Python 2 monolith into approximately 60 Python and Go services deployed on
GKE; playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Established a service template using Python/FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and
Terraform modules.
• Built an internal cost dashboard using Python, BigQuery billing exports and Looker Studio; rightsizing and
committed-use discounts reduced cloud spend by 31% (€4.2M per year).
• Led the platform organisation responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH 2015 – 2019
• Led technical work on the playback API using Python, Tornado and an internal framework similar to FastAPI,
with Cassandra and Redis.
• Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service for subscriptions, regions and devices using gRPC,
Cassandra, Redis and Kubernetes; it handled peak traffic of 120k requests per second with p99 latency under 15
ms.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart 2010 – 2015
• Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python,
PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led a team of six developers on the route-history product.
• Co-inventor of a granted patent for adaptive GPS sampling in vehicle fleets.
Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe 2005 – 2010
• Developed C++ and Python software for industrial data acquisition on Linux and embedded x86.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.
SELECTED PROJECTS & OPEN SOURCE
• Open-source maintainer, Python retry library (2012–2018): Maintained a library with approximately 1.5k
GitHub stars; used pytest and tox.
• Entitlement Service (Streamhaus, 2016–2017): Go, gRPC, Cassandra, Redis and Kubernetes; 120k requests per
second at peak.
• Monolith to Services Migration (Streamhaus, 2019–2023): Python, FastAPI, Go, GKE, Terraform,
OpenTelemetry and Prometheus.
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent to MSc), Computer Science | Rhine Valley University, 2005
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go, C++
Backend and APIs: FastAPI, Django, Flask, Tornado, asyncio, gRPC, Protobuf
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL, PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), Kubernetes, Terraform; AWS (EC2, S3)
Testing and observability: pytest, tox, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry
Other: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management
LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)
PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
• “Running Python at 100k rps” — conference talk, 2018
• “Cost is a feature” — internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role because it brings together production
backend engineering, dependable tracking services and practical work on event-driven systems.
Tessel’s focus on reducing the effort dispatchers spend chasing shipment updates makes the
reliability of its tracking platform especially meaningful.
I bring 21 years of experience building backend services and distributed systems in Python, Go and
C++. At Streamhaus, I designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service that handled 120,000
requests per second at peak, and led technical work on the playback API. I also helped migrate a
Python 2 monolith into around 60 Python and Go services, improving playback API availability
from 99.5% to 99.95%. Earlier, I built fleet-telematics systems ingesting GPS data from 300,000
vehicles, using Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ—a background closely related to
processing shipment events reliably.
My experience includes Python APIs, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing with pytest and tox,
and operating services with Kubernetes, Terraform and observability tooling. I have also
documented architecture and contributed to service standards and on-call guidelines. After leading
an engineering organisation, I am now looking to return to hands-on individual-contributor
backend work, where I can contribute directly to building and improving production services.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend and reliability experience could
contribute to Tessel’s Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.
With best regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
